questions.question: Crossover mirrors help the driver see:

options.text: The danger zones in front of the bus.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones in front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help the driver see the danger zone directly in front of a school bus. These mirrors also show danger zones on the left and right sides of the bus, from the front to the service door.

questions.question: Fueling a bus while passengers are on board is:

options.text: Acceptable only on trips longer than 100 miles.
Acceptable only if it cannot be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Acceptable only if it cannot be avoided.
questions.explanation: Do not fuel a bus while passengers are on board unless absolutely necessary. Never fuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: When stopped at a railroad crossing, a bus driver can hear if a train is coming by:

options.text: Waiting for passengers to be quiet on their own.

questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Look both ways for a train. Open the front door if it helps you see or hear an oncoming train.

questions.question: When driving a school bus, mirrors should be adjusted:
questions.explanation: Always check and adjust all mirrors before you start operating a school bus.

questions.question: If a student may have a back injury, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not move a student with a neck or spinal injury unless their life is in immediate danger.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is used to watch passenger activity inside the bus.

questions.question: The overhead inside rearview mirror should show:
questions.explanation: Position the top of the overhead mirror to show the top of the bus's rear window. This positioning allows you to see all students, including those sitting directly behind the driver.

questions.question: When dropping off students at a school, a driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition if leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine to secure the bus. Remove the key from the ignition if you leave the driver's seat. You must watch the students while they unload.

questions.question: Emergency roof hatches on a bus:

options.text: Can be open to allow fresh air while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be open to allow fresh air while driving.
questions.explanation: Some emergency roof hatches can be locked open to let in fresh air while driving. However, this should not be a regular practice.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse at a student pick-up point, you should:

options.text: Back up while students guide you.

questions.explanation: Backing up a school bus should be avoided. Do it only if there is no other safe way. If you must back up at a pick-up point, wait until all students have boarded first.

questions.question: Backing a school bus is:

options.text: Only to be done in the morning.

questions.explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged. Only back up if there is no safe alternative. If you must back up, follow all safety steps carefully.

questions.question: A posted speed limit for cars:

options.text: May be too fast for buses.
May be too slow for buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be too fast for buses.
questions.explanation: On curves especially, a speed limit that is safe for cars may be too fast for buses. Be extra careful when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: Students loading and unloading a bus:

options.text: Is simple and does not need to be supervised.
Can be dangerous and should be supervised.
May be done without the bus driver present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous and should be supervised.
questions.explanation: More students are hurt or killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Bus drivers must follow safety procedures during these times. Loading and unloading must always be supervised.

questions.question: Refueling a bus in an enclosed space, towing a bus with passengers, and talking with passengers are:
questions.explanation: Do not talk with passengers, fuel a bus inside a building, or tow a bus with riders inside. These are all prohibited practices.

questions.question: When inspecting the interior of a bus, you should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting the interior, make sure everything is safe and working. Check that each handhold and railing is secure and safe to use.

questions.question: Adjust a bus's mirrors:

options.text: At the first stoplight after starting your shift.

questions.explanation: Adjust and check mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the bus driver should:
questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors allow you to see all of the following, except:

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors show the area in front of the bus from the ground up to where you can see directly. They also show the front tires touching the ground and the area from the front to the service door. They do not show the tops of the rear tires.

questions.question: ABS helps you:

options.text: Keep your wheels from locking up.
Count the number of students boarding the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: The standee line:

options.text: Is a line that passengers should not cross.
Is a line upon which passengers should stand.
Is a line that should be used as passengers exit the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a line that passengers should not cross.
questions.explanation: On buses designed for standing passengers, no one may stand in front of the rear of the driver's seat. Buses must have a line on the floor showing where passengers cannot stand. This is called the standee line.
